seoTitle: Fix "Domain Locked at Registrar" Error (GoDaddy to Hostinger)
metaDescription: Stuck transferring your domain from GoDaddy to Hostinger due to a lock error? Learn how to unlock the domain, disable WHOIS protection, and retry.
intro: The "Domain is locked at the current registrar" error is one of the most common blockers when transferring a domain from GoDaddy to Hostinger, but it's usually a quick fix once you know where to look. This guide covers unlocking the domain, disabling WHOIS protection, and confirming eligibility before retrying the transfer.

steps.heading: Log in to your GoDaddy account
steps.body: Access your GoDaddy account and locate the domain showing the lock error during the transfer attempt.

steps.heading: Disable the domain lock
steps.body: Find the domain lock setting and turn it off, since a locked domain will always block a transfer request from completing.

steps.heading: Obtain the authorization (EPP) code
steps.body: Request the EPP code from GoDaddy, which Hostinger will need to verify and process the transfer.

steps.heading: Disable WHOIS protection if necessary
steps.body: Turn off WHOIS privacy protection temporarily, as it can sometimes interfere with the verification steps required for transfer.

steps.heading: Retry the domain transfer to Hostinger
steps.body: Once unlocked and with the EPP code in hand, go back to Hostinger and resubmit the domain transfer request.

faq.question: Why does GoDaddy show a domain lock error during transfer?
faq.answer: Domain locking is a default security feature that prevents unauthorized transfers, and it must be manually disabled before a transfer can proceed.

faq.question: Does disabling domain lock make my domain less secure?
faq.answer: Temporarily, yes, since it removes a layer of protection against unauthorized transfers, so it's best to complete the transfer soon after unlocking.

faq.question: What if the transfer still fails after unlocking?
faq.answer: Check that the EPP code is correct and that the domain meets any minimum registration age requirement, since these are other common transfer blockers.

faq.question: Do I need to disable WHOIS protection every time I transfer a domain?
faq.answer: Not always, but it can be a factor in some verification steps, so it's worth checking if the transfer is otherwise stuck.
